verification_status: Source-inspected, hashes/line spans checked; native reproduction not executed during construction.
reference_answer: At the frozen revision, SegmentImpl::Open recovers a writing block. recover() opens the existing log into local recover_wal_file, replays records through internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete, and closes the local handle on return. Internal insertion fills memory_store_, indexes, doc_ids_, and writing-block metadata, so the recovered data can initially be fetched and counted. Recovery does not restore wal_file_. Normal Insert instead calls append_wal, which lazily opens the member WAL before internal_insert. Optimize switches any nonempty writing segment via switch_to_new_segment_for_writing; that calls dump, which calls flush. flush returns OK immediately when wal_file_ is null or reports no records. In this scenario the member is null, so it skips memory/index persistence and finish_memory_components/update_version. dump still seals the segment, and the switch removes the old writing-forward-block metadata, installs a new writing segment, and applies/flushes that version. On a subsequent open the old block no longer participates in writing-block recovery, and its memory-only documents are not represented as properly persisted blocks. Stats sums live segment doc_ids_ and derives index completeness from indexed metadata, so same-handle healthy statistics and successful status do not prove the next open can reconstruct data. Restore the member-WAL lifecycle after replay (close the reader and reopen the existing WAL into wal_file_, checking errors) so normal flush can persist replayed data before switching. A regression must crash before flush, verify recovery, immediately optimize without additional writes, then close and reopen fresh and verify the known documents; a no-crash control distinguishes this from all unflushed data being unsafe.

criteria.claim: Recovery reconstructs readable in-memory state from a temporary/local WAL handle but finishes without installing/reopening the member wal_file_.
criteria.full_credit: Name the local-versus-member distinction and show replay enters internal operations that populate memory/doc ids. A generic claim of stale cache is insufficient.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for correct recovered-memory state or correct local/member WAL distinction, but not both.

criteria.claim: flush() treats a null member WAL or one with no records as no pending work, returning OK before persistence. Here the null member arm triggers.
criteria.full_credit: State the exact null-or-no-record guard, identify the null-member cause for this scenario, and explain the skipped persistence/finalization.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for identifying flush as the skipped step without the precise condition or lifecycle consequences.

criteria.claim: Optimize -> switch_to_new_segment_for_writing -> dump -> flush; successful early return allows sealing/switching and version persistence after old writing-block metadata is removed, so a future open cannot recover/persist the lost memory via the old writing block.
criteria.full_credit: Connect the full call chain to removal of old writing metadata and the new persisted version, rather than blaming vector-ranking quality or claiming optimize never calls flush.
criteria.partial_credit: 1 point for correct call chain without the metadata/reopen consequence, or correct consequence without the chain.

criteria.claim: Same-handle Stats reads in-memory segment counts and indexed metadata; success/index completeness is not a durability or data-content check.
criteria.full_credit: Explain doc_ids_ based counting and metadata-derived index completeness; do not invent a separate stats cache.

criteria.claim: Normal Insert appends to/opens the member WAL before internal_insert, unlike replay, explaining the no-crash control under the stated size assumptions.
criteria.full_credit: Cite ordinary insertion and append/open behavior; distinguish recovery bypassing append_wal.

criteria.claim: Restore the invariant that replayed pending data has an attached usable member WAL before later flush/dump; close the temporary reader and reopen/retain the existing WAL through the normal member path, handling errors.
criteria.full_credit: A minimal lifecycle repair equivalent to attaching/reopening the existing WAL is accepted. An alternative persistence design is accepted only if the answer proves it preserves version, flush and WAL cleanup invariants.
criteria.partial_credit: No partial point; simply calling public flush on the broken state is not a repair.

criteria.claim: Regression: insert known documents, force abrupt termination before flush, reopen and verify recovered data, optimize without extra writes, close, reopen from fresh process and compare count plus representative/all known documents and vectors. Include a no-crash or already-flushed control.
criteria.full_credit: Fresh reopen after optimize and no intervening writes are required, because same-handle checks and writes that lazily open the WAL can mask the defect. Executing the test is not required.

critical_contradictions: Claims WAL replay itself failed and documents never existed after initial reopen.
Claims optimize never invokes a flush path.
Claims simply calling flush() on this recovered state repairs the lifecycle without further changes.
Claims vector similarity/quantization or Python garbage collection is the causal defect.
Claims same-handle statistics prove disk durability.

evidence_spans.claim_supported: A writing block causes SegmentImpl::Open to recover it.
Recovery opens a local recover_wal_file and defers its close; it does not assign the member wal_file_.
Recovery dispatches records directly to internal insertion/update/upsert/delete methods.
Internal insertion creates/writes memory components and updates doc_ids_ and writing-block metadata.
Recovery finishes with Status::OK without attaching/reopening the member WAL.
Optimize switches a nonempty writing segment before planning compaction on persisted segments.
Segment switch dumps the old segment, removes its writing-forward-block metadata, installs new writing segment, and persists the new version.
dump calls flush before sealing; flush returns success immediately if member WAL is null or has no record.
The early return skips memory-store, scalar/FTS and vector-index flushes.
The normal flush finalizes memory components into persisted-block metadata and updates/flushed version.
Statistics count current segment objects and derive completeness from vector-indexed metadata.
Per-segment count is derived from in-memory doc_ids_, minus deletions.
Ordinary Insert calls append_wal before internal_insert.
open_wal_file installs wal_file_; append_wal opens it lazily before appending.
Successful finish_memory_components registers persisted scalar/vector blocks.
Existing pre-fix crash test verifies readback immediately after recovery but does not optimize and reopen.
